# Module 2: Understanding Floating-Point Arithmetic

## Module Arc

- A finite set represents a wide numeric range
- Each operation rounds
- Exceptional values carry information
- Evaluation order can change the result

::: notes
Use diagrams and live experiments when developing this section; avoid turning
the deck into an IEEE 754 encoding reference.
:::

## Predict Before Running

- When does `x + small == x`?
- Can a finite calculation produce infinity?
- Is `NaN == NaN`?
- Does `(a + b) + c` equal `a + (b + c)`?

::: notes
Collect predictions before showing results. Choose values that expose the
behaviour clearly in the eventual exercise language.
:::

## What To Observe

- Spacing grows with magnitude
- Rounding is unavoidable but structured
- Overflow and underflow affect intermediate values
- Real-number algebra is not always a safe rewrite rule

::: notes
End by asking how a difference should be measured. That question leads directly
to Module 3.
:::
